review_notes: I read the whole 23-line target file and the definition of `ratLocalizedAt` in Definitions/Def_GaloisRep_Flat.lean. I also grepped for uses of the membership lemmas in P2M/Sol. Neither lemma in the target has a simp attribute. Several other files redeclare the same Iff.rfl lemma privately and apply it with `rw`. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether `simp` can already unfold membership in `ratLocalizedAt p` by some other route. It probably cannot, because `ratLocalizedAt` is a plain `def`. I also did not check whether an `@[simp]` attribute here would conflict with the other copies of the lemma, which are declared in other namespaces or as private lemmas. The prime-hypothesis version `mem_ratLocalizedAt_iff` should not be tagged simp as written, since `hp` is an explicit hypothesis.

findings.excerpt:
theorem mem_ratLocalizedAt_iff_coprime {p : ℕ} (q : ℚ) :
    q ∈ ratLocalizedAt p ↔ q.den.Coprime p :=
  Iff.rfl
findings.problem: This is the canonical membership characterisation for the opaque `def ratLocalizedAt`, but it is not a simp lemma. It also lives in a `FlatSol` namespace in a solution file, not next to the definition. Because `ratLocalizedAt` is a plain `def` producing a `Subring`, `simp` has no way to turn `q ∈ ratLocalizedAt p` into a statement about `q.den`. Other files therefore redeclare the same `Iff.rfl` lemma privately and apply it by hand with `rw [mem_ratLocalizedAt_iff, ...]`. The result is several copies of one fact and no simp normal form for membership.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem GaloisRep.mem_ratLocalizedAt {p : ℕ} {q : ℚ} : q ∈ ratLocalizedAt p ↔ q.den.Coprime p := Iff.rfl` in Def_GaloisRep_Flat.lean, directly after the definition. The orientation is safe: the left side is a membership atom and the right side is a `Nat.Coprime` on `q.den`, so no cycle arises. Then replace the private copies (and this `mem_ratLocalizedAt_iff_coprime`) with `simp`/`simp only [GaloisRep.mem_ratLocalizedAt]`. Keep the prime-dependent form `¬ p ∣ q.den` non-simp, because it needs the explicit `hp : p.Prime` argument. A simp version of it would need a `[Fact p.Prime]` instance.
findings.benefit: Goals such as `(1 : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ ratLocalizedAt p` or `((q.den : ℤ) : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ ratLocalizedAt p` reduce under `simp` together with the existing `Rat` den lemmas. Downstream files no longer need local copies of the lemma or manual `rw` chains. There would be a single canonical normal form for membership.
